$comment: The auth-callback contract: which redirect destinations exist, per surface, and how a mobile confirmation callback is parsed. TypeScript (tests/unit/auth-redirect-contract.test.ts), Swift (AuthCallbackTests) and Kotlin (AuthCallbackLinkTest) all read this file directly, so the three platforms cannot drift apart on what they accept. Redirects are never taken from a client request: each surface uses only its own destination below, and each Supabase project's allow-list carries exactly its own environment's rows.

faithful.$comment: One custom scheme for every build, by construction: iOS and Android both register `faithful` and neither declares Universal/App Links (a deliberate decision recorded in Info.plist and AndroidManifest.xml). Environment separation happens at the identity provider, not in the URL: each environment talks to its own Supabase project, the PKCE verifier is stored per environment, and a code minted by one project is meaningless to another.

dashboard.$comment: The staging origin is a deployment decision this repository deliberately does not invent; its callback is <staging origin>/auth/callback.

vectors.$comment: accepted: exactly the mobile callback, carrying a code. failures: the mobile callback carrying a provider failure (or nothing) — parsed, shown as a typed state, never exchanged. rejected: not a mobile auth callback at all — including the dashboard callback, which must never be treated as one, and lookalikes a hostile link could carry. The parser returns nothing for these and the app does nothing.

accepted.why: scheme and host compare case-insensitively, as URLs do
extra parameters the provider appends are ignored, not fatal

failures.why: the provider reports failures in the fragment
and some versions report them in the query
a percent-encoded description must be parsed, not crash the parser: decoding it yields a space, which some URL APIs refuse as query input
the same shape a real provider sends, fully percent-encoded
a malformed percent escape is tolerated: the reason still reads, and nothing throws
our callback shape carrying neither a code nor an error is a broken link, shown as one
a code outside the contract bounds is refused before any network call
off-alphabet codes are refused before any network call

rejected.why: a different faithful deep link is not an auth callback
a destination link is not an auth callback
the dashboard callback must never be consumed by the mobile app
the development dashboard callback must never be consumed by the mobile app

dashboardRejected.why: the mobile callback must never be accepted as a dashboard post-auth destination
absolute URLs are never accepted as a dashboard destination
